title: Product of a quasi-coherent ideal and a quasi-coherent module: quasi-coherence and sections over affine opens
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal J\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ the cokernel of the inclusion, and $\mathcal J^1=\mathcal J$, $\mathcal J^{n+1}=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^n$. Then: (1) $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ are quasi-coherent, and every $\mathcal J^n$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals; (2) for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal J(U)\cdot\mathcal F(U)$ (the submodule of $\mathcal F(U)$ generated by the products $as$, $a\in\mathcal J(U)$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$), the map $\mathcal F(U)\to(\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F)(U)$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal J(U)\mathcal F(U)$, and $\mathcal J^n(U)=\mathcal J(U)^n$; (3) for every open $V\subseteq X$, $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)|_V=(\mathcal J|_V)(\mathcal F|_V)$ as submodules of $\mathcal F|_V$.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$. Restriction to $U$ preserves the relevant colimits, and the affine tilde/global-sections comparison identifies $\mathcal J|_U$ and $\mathcal F|_U$ with the tilde sheaves of the $R$-modules $I=\mathcal J(U)$ and $M=\mathcal F(U)$. Under these identifications the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ restricts to the tilde of the $R$-linear map $I\otimes_R M\to M$, $(a\otimes s)\mapsto as$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions, item (1)) and Lemma 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent); Modules, Lemma 01CE (lemma-tensor-product-permanence)

proof.text: Apply the quasi-coherent cokernel/image calculation to this multiplication map. Its image is $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ and is quasi-coherent, its cokernel is $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ and is quasi-coherent, and on the affine open $U$ the image is the submodule $I M\subseteq M$. Consequently $\mathcal F(U)\to(\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F)(U)$ is surjective with kernel $I M$, so $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal J(U)\mathcal F(U)$.

proof.text: The same argument proves the assertions for all powers by induction. For $n=1$ there is nothing to prove. If $\mathcal J^n$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and $\mathcal J^n(U)=I^n$, apply the preceding product/image calculation to $\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal J^n\to\mathcal J^n$ (viewing $\mathcal J^n$ as a quasi-coherent submodule of $\mathcal O_X$). Its image is $\mathcal J^{n+1}$, hence is quasi-coherent, and on $U$ its sections are $I I^n=I^{n+1}$. Thus every $\mathcal J^n$ is a quasi-coherent ideal and $\mathcal J^n(U)=\mathcal J(U)^n$.

proof.text: For any open $V\subseteq X$, the restriction of the image sheaf of the multiplication map to $V$ is the image sheaf of the restricted multiplication map: both consist of sections that are locally in the image on open neighbourhoods. Therefore $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)|_V=(\mathcal J|_V)(\mathcal F|_V)$ as submodules of $\mathcal F|_V$. The same local description also shows that the quotient map and its kernel restrict compatibly.
